svg.title: Kong on bare metal with Node.js in Docker — full architecture
svg.desc: Traffic flows from internet through firewall, hits Kong on port 8000 on the host, Kong proxies to Node.js containers via Docker port binding on 127.0.0.1:3000 and 3001

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Who sends requests to Kong in this Docker setup?')
sendPrompt('Why do we put UFW firewall in front of Kong?')

svg.text: Kong process (runs directly on host — NOT in Docker)

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What is Kong proxy port 8000 used for?')
sendPrompt('Why is the Kong Admin API on 127.0.0.1 and not 0.0.0.0?')
sendPrompt('What is the Kong status port 8100 used for?')
sendPrompt('What does the key-auth plugin do in Kong?')
sendPrompt('How does Kong rate limiting work?')
sendPrompt('What does the response transformer plugin do?')
sendPrompt('How do Kong health checks work?')
sendPrompt('What does Kong store in PostgreSQL?')
sendPrompt('How does deck gateway sync work with Kong?')

svg.text: containers talk to each other by service name internally

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does Docker port binding work and why can Kong reach the container via 127.0.0.1?')
g.text: Docker binds container :3000 → host 0.0.0.0:3000 · Kong reaches it at 127.0.0.1:3000

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the Node.js container receive requests from Kong?')
sendPrompt('Why does the second Node container use port 3001 on the host?')
sendPrompt('What endpoints does the Node.js app expose?')
sendPrompt('What does the GET /output endpoint return?')
sendPrompt('Why does the Node app need a /health endpoint for Kong?')
sendPrompt('What does GET /debug/headers show us about Kong?')
sendPrompt('What headers does Kong inject into the request before it reaches Node.js?')
g.text: Headers Kong injects (Node reads these — Kong strips the API key)

svg.text: Solid arrows = live traffic · Dashed arrows = config / admin
